jobs.jd:
Why join us 

 Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

 Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

 Engineering at Brex 

 Engineering at Brex is about building systems that scale with speed and intention. Our teams operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration, own outcomes end to end, and push for excellence from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft and builders grow by solving meaningful technical problems.

 What you’ll do 

 As a Senior GRC Engineer at Brex, you’ll lead the IT security compliance workstreams that connect our technical control owners to the people who examine our controls: external auditors, Internal Audit, state regulators, and Finance. You’ll coordinate and test the technical controls behind our financial reporting (SOX/ITGC), our annual SOC 1 Type 2 report, our state money transmitter examinations, and our FINRA IT requirements. You’ll also run the annual business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) testing calendar.

 As part of the GRC team you may also contribute to the following operational tasks:

- Third party risk management 

- Risk register maintenance and reporting

- Customer Trust / GTM due diligence support

- Tooling access requests

- Assist with requests related to other certifications like SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, or ISO 27001

 Where you’ll work 

 This role will be based in our Vancouver office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

 Responsibilities 

- Lead IT SOX/ITGC test procedures, walkthroughs, evidence, workpapers, and remediation across logical access, change management, computer operations, and IT governance.

- Manage our annual SOC 1 Type 2 engagement, including external auditor coordination, control descriptions, evidence, deficiency tracking, and review of draft report sections.

- Support state money transmitter (MTL) examinations by working with Legal, Compliance, and Finance on IT documentation, examiner requests, and tracking of IT findings.

- Test quarterly user access reviews, privileged-access evidence, and segregation-of-duties remediation, and verify that in-scope changes are complete and properly authorized.

- Run the annual BC/DR testing calendar, including tabletop and failover exercises, and document results, evidence, and remediation.

- Prepare FINRA-related IT control documentation, including business continuity, books-and-records, systems access reviews, and readiness testing.

- Track findings through to closure with clear control owners, deadlines, and evidence, and keep audit coordination separate from control operation.

- Support broader GRC team operational tasks related to evidence collection, access requests, and risk management.

 Requirements 

- 5+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX/ITGC testing, GRC, or technology compliance, in fintech, financial services, or public accounting.

- Hands-on experience with ITGC testing across logical access, change management, and computer operations, and with documenting results in audit workpapers.

- Working knowledge of SOC 1 / SSAE 18, including Type 2 reports, control descriptions, and deficiency management.

- Familiarity with PCAOB standards.

- Experience working with external auditors, regulators, or examiners and responding to their requests on deadline.

- Strong organization and project management skills, with the ability to run several audit workstreams on different calendars at once.

- Clear communication, and comfort holding technical control owners accountable for evidence and remediation.

 As part of the GRC team you may also contribute to the following operational tasks:

 Responsibilities

- Prepare FINRA-related IT control documentation, including business continuity, books-and-records, systems access reviews, and readiness testing.

- Working knowledge of SOC 1 / SSAE 18, including Type 2 reports, control descriptions, and deficiency management.

- Experience working with external auditors, regulators, or examiners and responding to their requests on deadline.

- Clear communication, and comfort holding technical control owners accountable for evidence and remediation.

 Bonus points

- Experience with GRC or audit workflow tools, or with SQL or scripting for control testing.

ABOUT THE TEAM
 The mission of the UI Test team is to ensure best-in-class UI experience for Rubrik products. The team accomplishes this by testing and automating customer workflows, providing UI automation infrastructure for end to end validation and benchmarking, checking usability and user experience and consistency across the features and products. Key stakeholders are product component teams, product management, release managers and end customers.

 The key responsibilities of the team include qualifying new features for production release and leading UI release regression qualification across Rubrik's on-prem and cloud products. We do manual and automated testing, including developing the test infrastructure needed. We build and use AI-native skills that automate the entire testing lifecycle, starting from generating the UI test plan to executing them in real environments. 

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 UI Test team responsibilities: 

- Feature qualification:

- The UI Test team qualifies new features from the end-user point of view (UI) for all Rubrik products before rolling out to production. We make sure every feature adheres to the quality standards and integrates well with the rest of the product. 

- Maintains high quality bar in test processes, strategy and test execution.

- Release regression testing: 

- 

- All released features are regression tested in every release, on a cadence that depends on the product, with both manual and automated UI testing.

- Automation: 

- New features enter the automation backlog after release and are picked up by priority. UI Automation using browser automation frameworks such as Playwright. 

- Infrastructure automation/maintenance using Python.

- Automated test pipelines in a CI/CD system

- Each phase of the testing life cycle is getting automated. Using AI-assisted tooling to generate test cases from product artifacts, execute them against real environments to reduce manual qualification effort.

 QUALIFICATIONS: 

- Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field

- 5-8 years of experience in software testing, UI testing and automation

- Solid understanding on data protection, storage, security, virtualization, databases, cloud, kubernetes and generative AI

- Familiarity with UI performance and accessibility testing.

- Working knowledge of microservices, API, cloud native architectures and how to test them

- Experience with Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), cybersecurity, AI resilience. A cloud certification is an advantage.

- Deep experience in driving complete test life cycle (test planning, execution, automation) and release qualification. Test management using TestRail or equivalent is a plus.

- Good hands-on experience programming in Python or equivalent and UI automation using TestIM, Selenium, Playwright or equivalent. JavaScript/TypeScript knowledge is a plus.

- Hands-on experience using AI coding or testing assistants in test authoring, debugging or automation, and sound judgment about the quality of their output.

- Hands on experience in creating, triaging and maintaining automated test pipeline using Jenkins, GitHub or similar CI/CD tools

- Strong written and verbal communication, including documentation that others can pick up without a handoff.

 Key differentiating factors: 

- Due to the unique placement of the team, it is exposed to multiple key technologies of Rubrik products. 

- This opportunity is not just another manual testing or automation role, key factor is the exposure and opportunity to learn core technologies of data protection, storage, security, anti ransomware, Virtualization(Hyper-V, VMware), Databases (SQL, Oracle, Mongo, DB2), cloud technologies (Azure, Google, AWS), Kubernetes, and cutting edge features involving Generative AI etc.

- Exposure to automated infrastructure creation and clean up on various platforms like VMware, Azure, AWS etc.

- Hands-on work with AI-based tools for test authoring, execution and automation.

- Automation using latest AI based tools 

- Every team member is given equal opportunity to lead releases on a rotational basis giving them opportunities to learn the release process and develop their leadership skills.

- Ownership opportunities: every member in the team irrespective of the designation has end-end ownership right from PRD review, test case development, interaction with key stakeholders( like Product manager, program managers, component managers and developers), execution and reporting

- Opportunity to become a quality advocate for the assigned component and product, and develop expertise in the assigned areas.

- This is a high visibility team as every feature of every product of the company has to be qualified by this team

When millions of builders ship their Lambda functions, it all just works — in seconds, anywhere in the world. The machinery that makes that possible is the control plane: the systems that validate, orchestrate, and propagate every function's state so the data plane can execute it flawlessly at any scale.

You'll own the full path from API request to running function. About Us

 At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

 At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

 Available Locations: Lisbon, or London (Hybrid) 

About the Department

 Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Rather than being constrained by the structures which make Cloudflare a hugely successful business, we are able to leverage them to deliver entirely new tools and products to our customers. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.

About the Team

 We build the infrastructure that makes the web Payable , powering the future of machine-to-machine commerce.

 Here at Cloudflare, agentic commerce is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet . As AI agents increasingly navigate, consume, and act on the web, standard payment and authorization models built for humans are breaking down. We build tools that make the new internet payable by giving our users the ability to monetize access to their content, data, services, products, and outcomes across the Internet, regardless of where they are hosted.

jobs.jd:
About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the Role 

 Anthropic manages one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute.

 As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around one of Anthropic’s largest areas of spend.

 You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment.

 This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap: 

- Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need.

- Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other.

- Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number.

- Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO.

 Key responsibilities 

- Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs.

- Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Utilization improvements are worth enormous sums at our scale.

- Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline.

jobs.jd:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Design Systems Engineer to be one of the few engineers building the components that every Ramp product team uses — the person who makes our design system real in code. You’ll work in close partnership with our design systems lead and designers: they decide what the rules are, and you decide how to enforce them. Sometimes that’s a component that won’t allow a bad pattern. Sometimes it’s a codebase move that makes the right path the easy one. Sometimes it’s automation that catches drift before it spreads.

With AI agents now writing much of the UI, this role is also at the frontier of a changing craft. You’ll help decide what the system has to guarantee when humans and agents are both building on top of it — because agents don’t settle for the happy path, and the system needs to hold up either way.

Having worked as a designer (or deeply alongside one), you understand the design-eng collaboration challenges firsthand. You’re driven to improve it because you’ve lived with the pain points. You excel in UI and accessible design, prefer working directly in-browser, and get excited about emerging CSS properties.

This is an IC role on a small team, which means you’ll have real say in architecture, API design, and the tradeoffs that shape how Ramp builds — foundational, detail-obsessed frontend work with an outsized impact on every screen we ship.


What You’ll Do

 - Build and evolve the components and APIs that every product team at Ramp depends on

 - Make the enforcement call: when to encode a rule in the component itself, when to leave it to guidance, and when to invest in automation that catches drift

 - Partner with our design systems lead and designers to turn UX patterns and principles into working, consistent components

 - Shape the system so it holds up when both engineers and AI agents are building on it

 - Contribute to internal tooling and infrastructure that keeps velocity high without sacrificing quality

 - Champion the user experience and accessibility of our products, and keep the quality bar high

 - Help designers and engineers across Ramp ship faster with elegant, consistent component APIs and a focus on developer experience

 - Advocate for users by continuously iterating on our core products and experiences

 - Participate in day-to-day team rituals like design crit, story creation, and weekly stand-ups

 - Help us hire and grow the team to bring more craft and more perspectives to the work
   

What You Need

 - Tech/startup or digital product agency experience, or equivalent

 - A strong frontend engineer who could pass any engineering loop at Ramp — real hands-on skill, not just prompting AI to write code

 - Experience building design system components and APIs, not only consuming them

 - Excellent front-end development skills in semantic HTML, CSS (up to date on latest features) and JavaScript (and frameworks, pref. React)

 - Ability to drive implementation end to end, with sound UX and system design sense

 - Strong understanding of Product Design software (pref. Figma) and visual/interaction design principles

 - Strong organizational skills and a love for documentation

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a willingness to push back with reasons — e.g., when encoding a rule in a component would slow everyone down

 - Care for the details: motion, states, accessibility, and the small decisions that make a system feel coherent
   

Nice to Haves

 - Design systems experience from before AI tooling took off

 - Ability to articulate complex concepts to technical and non-technical peers

 - Solid understanding of accessibility development practices




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agent Eval Platform
jobs.jd:
The Role 
 Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. That makes the central problem of our team an unusually hard measurement problem: how do you score what an agent did — across a multi-step trajectory through a world it changed — precisely enough that the score can teach it to do better? 
 That signal is what this role owns. You'll build the judgement layer of our agent evaluation platform: the rubrics, the judges, the calibration against human labels, the methodology that makes a score mean something. And the payoff is larger than a report card — a judge good enough to grade a trajectory is a judge good enough to train against . The same calibrated signal that explains why an agent failed becomes the reward signal that stops it failing.
 This isn't a pretraining role, and it isn't a testing role. It's applied ML at a point where the methodology genuinely isn't settled: LLMs judging LLMs is an open research problem, and we're working it against agents that take real, irreversible actions in stateful, multi-tenant enterprise environments.

 What you get to do in this role: 
 We're hiring across three areas. You'll anchor on one and touch the others; which one is a conversation we have with you, not a slot we drop you into.
 Eval orchestration at scale 
 
- The runtime that executes multi-turn agent scenarios end-to-end — stand up the environment and user simulator, drive the user↔agent↔world loop, collect transcripts, traces, and final state, run validators and scoring, tear down

- Scheduling, retries, high-concurrency execution, and run isolation at production dataset sizes

- Versioned specs, datasets, and reports, with run-to-run comparison as a first-class operation

- Consolidating evals that run today as one-off workflows onto a single orchestration service — one source of truth, one place to schedule and retry

- Establishing a reliability floor and an SLO for the harness itself

- Getting to self-serve, so any team runs an eval without bespoke integration
 Agent observability and tracing 
 
- Leading the move to OpenTelemetry-native observability for the agent platform, replacing the parallel per-service logging, correlation, and redaction mechanisms in use today

- The span data model for agent trajectories — prompts, tool calls, plan updates, outcomes — so a trajectory is queryable , not reconstructed by hand from log files

- Trace context propagation across async boundaries and sessions that stay alive for minutes or hours

- Making full prompts and completions survive the pipeline intact, and keeping eval traffic from contaminating its own data

- Fault attribution and cross-run diffing: which component actually broke, and what changed since the last green run

- The debug surface support and harness engineers use, and the tracing contract with the team that builds the agent
 Stateful simulation 
 
- The simulation environment itself: stateful fakes of the enterprise systems agents call — ITSM, HR, knowledge bases, inventory — backed by a real datastore that persists changes during a run, so a created ticket is visible to a later read

- Per-run data injection and programmatic setup/teardown so every run is hermetic and repeatable

- LLM-driven user simulators for open-ended personas, and scripted state-machine simulators for deterministic flows

- Contract-testing mocks against real API schemas in CI, so simulation fidelity can't quietly drift as vendor APIs change

- Ahead of us: isolated sandbox environments reproducing the config, identity, search content, and permissions an agent actually reads — provisioned from an identical baseline and torn down every run
 And across all three: laying the foundation for using eval signal to optimize the agent, not just measure it.

To be successful in this role you have: 
 
 Experience in at least 3 of these: 
 
- Distributed systems: idempotency, delivery guarantees, isolation, and — unusually central here — determinism and reproducibility

- Orchestration and workflow runtimes: DAG execution, scheduling, retries, backfills, high-concurrency job systems (Temporal, Airflow, Argo, or something you built yourself)

- Observability internals as a builder , not just a user: OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors, semantic conventions, span context propagation, high-cardinality trace data

- Concurrent and async programming: Python asyncio, Go concurrency, structured cancellation

- Data-intensive pipelines: high-volume ingest, schema evolution, sampling and retention trade-offs

- gRPC/protobuf service and interface design
 Required: 
 
- 0-2 years building production backend or infrastructure systems

- Strong in Python or Go (ideally both)

- Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale

- Comfort making a non-deterministic system measurable. You don't need an ML background — but you should find it interesting to turn fuzzy agent behavior into a signal engineers are willing to gate releases on

- Comfort with ambiguity; these are novel problems without textbook solutions

 About the role 

 As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

 The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

 You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

 We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

 The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time. 

 What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

 This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

As an Applied AI Engineer, you will partner directly with Digital Native companies to design, build and deploy AI-powered products and systems. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

- Build and extend authorization systems that support custom roles, resource-aware access control, and secure defaults for product teams.

- Lead creation of durable, identity-aware audit trails and attribution for user, service, delegated, and agent-driven actions.

- Partner closely with engineers across Brex to make IAM integrations secure by default and easier to adopt through clear patterns, tooling, and shared libraries.

- Mentor engineers on the team to deliver high-quality code and produce operational improvements that raise the bar for reliability and maintainability across the team’s systems.

 Requirements 

- You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building reliable production backend systems.

- You have experience leading complex projects and mentoring other engineers.

- You have strong API design fundamentals, rigor around testing, code quality, and documentation.

- You understand core IAM concepts such as authentication, authorization, sessions, tokens, MFA, SSO, OAuth, SAML, OIDC, or RBAC.

- You communicate clearly, collaborate well across teams, and are effective in cross-functional technical discussions.

- You care about operational excellence and know how to improve system reliability, reduce toil, and maintain high-quality services over time.

- You have strong product and engineering judgment and can balance security, usability, and developer experience.

 Bonus points

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

There is only one Data Cloud. Snowflake’s founders started from scratch and designed a data platform built for the cloud that is effective, affordable, and accessible to all data users. But it didn’t stop there. They engineered Snowflake to power the Data Cloud, where thousands of organizations unlock the value of their data with near-unlimited scale, concurrency, and performance. This is our vision: a world with endless insights to tackle the challenges and opportunities of today and reveal the possibilities of tomorrow.

Our product offering runs on multiple cloud providers, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. Our infrastructure self-optimizes and provides high availability and data protection across cloud providers, so our users can focus on using their data, not managing it.

Our team is the Compute Service team. We build and operate the systems that schedule and run warehouse-backed work beyond a user’s interactive query: asynchronous and scheduled compute, elastic capacity for parts of live queries, and the scheduling control plane those workloads run on. We balance usability, performance, cost, and reliability for the teams and customers that depend on this compute.



We are actively hiring talented distributed systems developers. This role is an opportunity to shape the architecture and operation of core services that the rest of Snowflake runs on.


AS A SENIOR DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS ENGINEER AT SNOWFLAKE YOU WILL:

 - Solve real business needs at large scale by applying software engineering and analytical problem solving.

 - Design and implement scalable distributed systems for scheduling, queueing, dispatch, and completion of warehouse-backed work.

 - Analyze fault tolerance, high availability, performance, and scale challenges, and solve them.

 - Build admission control, isolation, and capacity management so shared compute stays fair and predictable.

 - Lead cross-functional initiatives, and collaborate with engineers, product managers, and technical program managers across teams.

 - Judge trade-offs among consistency, durability, latency, and cost, and build systems that meet the demands of rapidly growing services.

 - Ensure operational readiness of the services, and meet commitments to customers on availability and performance.


OUR IDEAL DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS ENGINEER WILL HAVE:

 - Substantial industry experience designing, building, and supporting large-scale systems in production.

 - Experience building large-scale, distributed, fault-tolerant services and control planes, including compute placement, queueing, and monitoring.

 - A strong understanding of operating-system concepts, including multi-threading, memory management, networking, storage, performance, and scale.

 - Strong computer-science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems.

 - Systems programming skills, including multi-threading and concurrency. Fluency in Java is preferred.

 - A track record of identifying problems and implementing creative solutions.

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.

 - A BS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience. An advanced degree is a plus.


WHY JOIN THE ENGINEERING TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

 - Build an industry-leading cloud data platform.

 - Solve challenging technical problems in parallel and distributed systems, resource management, scheduling, and large-scale system operation.

 - Work closely with partner teams, understand their use cases and needs, and choose the right problem to solve at the right time.

 - Contribute to a highly scalable and reliable cloud platform that runs on a very large fleet of machines, and to the Java systems that schedule and execute work on it.

 - Join a world-class team of industry veterans and rising engineers.





Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.



About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.



This role is based in Sydney, Australia. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees



In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

The Privacy Engineering team builds secure, reliable systems that help OpenAI meet its legal obligations while protecting user data. We’re looking for a full-stack Software Engineer to build the internal tools and data pipelines that power lawful data access request workflows and Legal Operations. You will work across product and data systems to make authorized retrieval and case handling accurate, efficient, and auditable. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys translating ambiguous operational requirements into durable systems, cares deeply about sensitive-data handling, and wants to improve both technical reliability and the day-to-day experience of the people operating these workflows.

 - Design, build, and operate backend systems and workflow tooling for the full lifecycle of lawful data access requests, from intake and scoping through authorized retrieval, review, preparation, and audit.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and interfaces across products and data stores so authorized teams can locate and handle the right records accurately and reproducibly.

 - Implement least-privilege access, approval gates, provenance, audit trails, data minimization, and safe failure modes for sensitive workflows.

 - Partner with Legal and Legal Operations to translate legal and operational requirements into clear technical designs and intuitive operator experiences.

 - Identify responsible automation opportunities that reduce repetitive work while preserving human review, judgment, and accountability.

 - Own production systems through testing, observability, incident response, documentation, and continuous reliability improvements.

 - Help define the architecture and roadmap for reusable privacy and legal-infrastructure foundations as OpenAI’s products and obligations evolve.

 - Have experience building or operating systems for lawful data access requests and understand the domain’s legal-process lifecycle, privacy and security constraints, auditability requirements, and operational sensitivities.

 - Ability to reason carefully about correctness, authorization, security, and privacy when working with sensitive data.

 - End-to-end ownership, including operating what you build, and comfort learning unfamiliar products and domains.

Who we are

 About Stripe 

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 

 Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.

 Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.

 Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue.

What you’ll do

 As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.

 You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve.

 Responsibilities 

- Build and operate reliable, low-latency services that detect and prevent fraud and abuse at scale

- Design APIs and dashboard experiences that help businesses investigate threats, configure defenses, and understand how Radar protects them

- Develop the shared platform and infrastructure that enable teams to build and launch new Radar capabilities

- Work directly with users to understand emerging threats and turn those insights into broadly useful products

- Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to bring new signals, models, and AI capabilities into production

- Own projects end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and iteration

- Uphold a high bar for engineering quality, reliability, and product craft while moving quickly as threats evolve

Who you are

 We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 

- 2+ years of industry software engineering experience

- Strong coding skills in any programming language, with experience building and maintaining production software

- Ability to work across systems and technologies, learn unfamiliar codebases, and make thoughtful technical trade-offs

- A rigorous approach to problem solving, including using data to investigate issues and evaluate whether a solution works

- Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across disciplines and contribute to your peers’ success

- An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems

 Preferred qualifications 

- Experience building distributed systems or real-time services with demanding reliability and latency requirements

- Experience building APIs, developer platforms, or intuitive user interfaces for complex workflows

- Experience bringing ML or AI capabilities into production software

- Experience working on fraud prevention, abuse prevention, risk, or security

- Experience taking a product from an early idea to launch and iterating directly with customers

About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

 The Endpoint team (Client Platform Engineering) manages the devices Anthropic’s people work on, plus the infrastructure underneath them. We treat the fleet as a distributed platform, not a collection of devices, and configuration ships as code through pull requests, CI, staging, and a canary group. Today the fleet is mostly macOS, with a growing mobile footprint.

 Anthropic also works with vendor and business process outsourcing (BPO) partners whose teams need access to Anthropic systems. Those programs are growing, in more countries and with more vendors. Anthropic-owned Chromebooks issued to vendor staff are becoming the default device for vendor teams. This role exists to make ChromeOS a supported platform with a dedicated owner. You will own ChromeOS end to end, from how devices are bought and enrolled to how they are locked down, monitored, and retired, and help bring Android in as a second platform.

 The team is deliberately lean and runs with high autonomy. You’ll define what ChromeOS looks like at Anthropic and own the platform decisions that get it there.

Responsibilities

- Own ChromeOS as a platform at Anthropic: device standards, Google Admin console and Chrome Enterprise setup, organizational unit design, and policy

- Manage ChromeOS policy as code through the Chrome Policy API, GAM, and Terraform, in the team's config-as-code pipeline, so changes are reviewed, tested, and progressively rolled out like the rest of the fleet

- Build zero touch enrollment through resellers, so a Chromebook arrives enrolled and works the first time in every country our vendor partners work from

- Work with IT Operations and procurement partners on buying and shipping devices internationally, including regions our current partners don’t reach

- Design device models for vendor teams (kiosk, managed guest sessions, shared devices, and assigned devices) and pick the right one for each program

- Work with Security on the contractor access model and on keeping Anthropic data off vendor devices

- Run data loss controls through Chrome Enterprise Premium

- Work with Security on the vendor identity model: which accounts vendor staff use and in which tenant

- Support Android as a second platform, working with the corporate mobile program on Android Enterprise and zero-touch enrollment

- Have owned ChromeOS as a platform for a fleet of thousands of devices

- Have automated ChromeOS policy through the Chrome Policy API or GAM

- Have run kiosk, managed guest, or shared device programs for frontline, contact center, or outsourced teams

- Have set up zero touch enrollment with resellers and shipped devices across several countries

- Have worked with Android device management and can hold your own in a mixed fleet

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Getting paid is still one of the most manual parts of running a business. Finance teams chase invoices over email, match payments to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and close the books late because cash data is scattered across banks, payment processors, and ERPs.

Ramp's Accounts Receivable team is building the system that automates all of it, from the moment an invoice is sent to the moment cash is reconciled in the general ledger. We own the full receivables lifecycle: invoicing, collections, payments, cash application, and accounting sync.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own core pieces of that system. The work sits where hard engineering problems meet real money: matching messy payment data to the right invoices, keeping ledgers correct to the cent, and syncing reliably with the accounting systems our customers depend on. You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

 - Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

 - Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

 - Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

 - Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 - Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship
   


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push back when the spec is wrong

 - Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

 - Strong system design judgment and the ability to balance speed, correctness, reliability, and simplicity

 - A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

 - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to technical decisions
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, or other financial workflows

 - Experience building integrations that keep data consistent across systems

 - Experience improving reliability and operational visibility in a growing product




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)
